extracted.intended_audience: public relations counsels / press agents / communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for public relations practitioners on analyzing publics, creating news/events, and working ethically and effectively with the press and other media. Covers tactics (stereotypes, committees, headlines), news-value, channel selection, verification, and literary quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze the public
rubrics_metrics.description: He must analyze the public he is trying to reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualize oneself as belonging to many publics and subdivisions (manufacturer, retailer, importer, employer, worker, financier, politician, etc.); estimate interaction between the public and the client; determine which sections of the public must be reached and generalize as far as possible to strike on the appeals of groups which will be influential within society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devise a plan of action and select distribution organs
rubrics_metrics.description: He must devise a plan of action for the client to follow and determine the methods and the organs of distribution available for reaching his public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide methods/channels (press, radio, lecture, advertising, mail, stage, word of mouth, pulpit, schoolroom, legislative chamber) and plan steps the client will take to reach target publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use stereotypes and representative committees to mirror publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use stereotypes; organize committees or bodies reflecting a cross section of influential community members (banker, society woman, prominent lawyer, preacher) to reenforce impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For a hotel's anniversary form an anniversary committee of leading businessmen and stereotypical figures so that the hotel is identified with respected group types; stereotypes concrete and reenforce otherwise indefinite impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to instincts and universal desires
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal to the instincts and the universal desires is the basic method through which he produces his results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilize appeals to desires/instincts discussed earlier and characteristics of group formation; these are primary means to secure acceptance and favorable reactions from the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the issue easy to pick out — overcome public attention 'flicker'
rubrics_metrics.description: He must make it easy for the public to pick his issue out of the great mass of material; overcome 'the tendency on the part of public attention to "flicker" and "relax."'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do for the public mind what the newspaper does with headlines: present compact, vivid simplifications and visuals so the idea stands out among competing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify and dramatize abstract discussions and heavy facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract discussions and heavy facts are the groundwork of his analysis, but they cannot be given to the public until they are simplified and dramatized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refinements of reason and shadings of emotion rarely reach a considerable public; lift startling facts and isolate ideas and develop them into events that are more readily understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create news — be a creator of events
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel, therefore, is a creator of news for whatever medium he chooses to transmit his ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lift startling facts from the subject, isolate ideas, develop them into events; construct and stage events (celebrations, contests, demonstrations, launches, banquets) designed to have 'carrying capacity' in chosen media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use headlines and visual metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: The headline is a compact, vivid simplification of complicated issues. The cartoon provides a visual image which takes the place of abstract thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft concise headline-like statements or visual symbols to encapsulate your issue; use physical metaphors to objectify human qualities so the public can readily visualize and remember them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crystallize obscure tendencies and create resonant symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: His capacity for crystallizing the obscure tendencies of the public mind before they have reached definite expression is what makes him valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create symbols the public is ready to respond to; analyze reactions, find individual and community stereotypes that will bring favorable responses; speak in the language of the audience to secure favorable reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and apply news-value factors
rubrics_metrics.description: News value consists of multiple characteristics (e.g., timeliness, departure from the established order, familiarity, personal effect, importance of persons/activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: (1) timeliness/freshness; (2) departure from established order (what disturbs routine); (3) readers' familiarity with subject/persona; (4) effect on readers' personal concerns; (5) general importance of persons or activities affected. Tailor pitches to maximize these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide truthful, accurate, and verifiable material
rubrics_metrics.description: It is because he acts as the purveyor of truthful, accurate and verifiable news to the press that the conscientious and successful counsel on public relations is looked upon with favor by the journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material must be carefully prepared and as accurately verified as if the editor had assigned a reporter; avoid falsehoods and ensure facts are corroborated to retain editors' trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor material to the particular newspaper, department, and editor
rubrics_metrics.description: It must suit the particular needs of each particular newspaper and, even more than that, it must suit the needs of the particular editor in whose department it is hoped that it will be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match content, angle, tone, and format to the paper's departments (news, editorial, women's, society, sports, financial, etc.) and to the expectations of the specific editor you are targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure high literary and journalistic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The literary quality of the material must be up to the best standards of the profession of journalism. The writing must be good, in the particular sense in which each newspaper considers a story well written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare copy as if assigned to a staff reporter; clarity, style, and professional craft matter to secure placement and maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use overt acts or manifest events to create publishable news
rubrics_metrics.description: An overt act is often necessary before an event can be regarded as news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News typically requires a definite, manifest act (bankruptcy, fire, collision, arrest, speech, vote, meeting); rumors or vague background are insufficient — produce or wait for a definable occurrence that editors can report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know where newspapers find news — monitor beats and public offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain places are watched constantly or regularly by metropolitan dailies (Police Headquarters, Courts, Stock Exchange, City Hall, Coroner's Office, Morgue, Shipping/Immigration offices, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of press beats and institutional records; use those channels or create events that will appear on the radar of reporters and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use diverse media and adapt approach to each medium
rubrics_metrics.description: There is, of course, first and perhaps most important, the press. There is the moving picture; the lecture platform; advertising; direct-by-mail; the stage—drama and music; word of mouth; the pulpit, the schoolroom, the legislative chamber; radio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand medium-specific constraints and opportunities (e.g., radio controllers may insist on presenting all points of view for partisan matters; propose symposiums or authoritative speakers for broadcasts). Choose media that best reach the target public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct events tailored to a medium's 'carrying capacity'
rubrics_metrics.description: The launching of battleships with ceremony; the laying of corner stones; the presentation of memorials; demonstration meetings, parties and banquets are all events created with a view to their carrying capacity in the various mediums that reach the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design events with elements that translate well into the chosen mediums — visuals for photography, spectacle for news columns, human-interest angles for feature pages, sound bites for radio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain highest moral and technical standards to retain editors' trust
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel could not possibly succeed unless he complied with the highest moral and technical requirements of those with whom he is working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are suspicious and remember errors; a single spurious or fraudulent item can be fatal to reputation. Prioritize truthfulness, accuracy, and ethical conduct to preserve long-term relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid presenting rumors; provide definite publishable facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from libel concerns, rumors provide nothing definite on which to peg a story — there must be a manifestation and an event must assume a definable shape before it becomes news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pitch speculation; secure or create definite facts or overt acts that editors can verify and publish. Where background exists, try to create a consequent overt event to make it newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use respected third parties/stereotyped authorities to lend credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A committee of nationally known sales-managers is chosen to act as judges for the contest and immediately success is assured. The stereotype has bespoken the value of the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage known authorities, reputable judges, or recognizable community stereotypes to confer legitimacy and newsworthiness on contests, events, or claims.
